The 'first edition ... Biskra ... October 1st & 2nd' Facebook text the earlier research found is from 2018 (ALCPC 2018 at Univ. Biskra, 1-2 Oct 2018, 160 students/32 universities, ~40 teams, Sofrecom co-organiser), not 2024/25. The last ALCPC with any web footprint is 2022 (El Oued, 10-11 Oct 2022; winner Univ. Biskra, ESI 2nd and 3rd). No ALCPC 2023 or 2024 trace in Algerian university news, Codeforces, FR/AR/EN news, or LinkedIn via search. Series appears dormant after 2022; the 2024 CMS/finder entry is an empty placeholder.

evidence.what_it_says: No ALCPC/Algeria event listed; 2024 national contests shown are AoLCPC2024 (Angola, Oct 10-11), LCPC2024 (Lebanon, Oct 4-5), QCPC2024 (Qatar, Sep 27-28); 'no upcoming events'.

'Pour sa première édition en Algérie, ALCPC ... organisé les 1er et 2 octobre 2018 à l'Université de Biskra' with 160 students from 32 universities; 5 teams qualified for the regional final in Egypt (9-13 Nov). Establishes that the Biskra 'first edition / Oct 1-2' text is 2018, not 2024.

Algerian national qualifiers held 1-2 Oct 2018 at the central library of Mohamed Khider University of Biskra, organised by the Biskra Computer Science Club with the 'BISKRA READS' association; about 40 teams; judges from Tunisia and Egypt.
ALCPC 2022 qualifiers 'will be held at EL-Ouad University on October 10 and 11, 2022'; regional final in Egypt 9-13 Nov; registration via icpc.global/regionals/finder/ALCPC-2022.

The competition concluded Tuesday 11 Oct 2022 at Univ. Chahid Hamma Lakhdar (El Oued); University of Biskra team 1st, ESI (National Higher School of Computer Science) 2nd and 3rd. Last documented ALCPC edition.
Overview of Algerian ICPC participation (ESI, USTHB, ESTIN 'regularly advance to the ICPC Africa and Arab regional finals'); does not mention ALCPC at all - no 2024 national contest cited.

series_level_findings: SEERC: the official per-year static sites at https://seerc.icpc.global/<year>/ (1995-2024) are LIVE and fetchable with this environment's WebFetch (the catalogue fetcher's 403 is client-specific; the host rate-limits parallel fetches, so capture one page at a time). Each year from ~2000 has a navigati.htm hub linking report.htm (final report: exact contest date, host building, registered/accepted team counts by country, top-3 with member names and coaches), results.htm (standings), problems.htm, photos.htm, sponsors.htm; 1995-1999 use result95.htm / result96.htm / standings97.htm / standings99.htm. All ten target years are confirmed by these pages. Catalogue date errors: the contest day was the SATURDAY in 2000 (Oct 21), 2001 (Oct 20), 2003 (Oct 18), 2004 (Oct 16) and 2013 (Oct 12); the catalogue has the Sunday for each. Host for every year 1999-2013 was the Dept. of Computer Science and Engineering, Politehnica University of Bucharest (Rectorat building; AN building in 2004); 1995-1997 were run by the ACM Romanian Chapter in Bucharest (Microsoft-sponsored). Multi-site with Vinnytsia NTU from 2011 (2011, 2012, 2013 and 2016 reports/articles). The root https://seerc.icpc.global/ now redirects to https://seerc.euc.icpc.global/ (SEERC 2026: Thessaloniki/U. of Macedonia + Kyiv/KSE; RD Alexandros Spitalas, co-RD Kostas Tsichlas; history menu links only 2021-2025). Useful series context: Codeforces entry 2882 (SEERC 2011 multi-site judging failure and ICPC Appeals Committee ruling), entry 9207 (SEERC 2013 participant account), vntu.edu.ua/en/acm (2011-2012 Vinnytsia reports). UPM (Slovenia): continuous since at least 2003 (UP FAMNIT), results were on upm.si (dead; first Wayback capture 2011-12-14) and now tekmovanja.acm.si (history from 2012). Southern Subregional (Saratov): neerc.ifmo.ru/archive/<year>/southern/standings.html holds static standings for 2017 and 2019 but not 2018/2020; the host site icpc.sgu.ru is robots-blocked here but archived in Wayback. ALCPC (Algeria): editions documented 2018 (Biskra) and 2022 (El Oued); nothing for 2023-2025, and ACPC's own calendar omits Algeria in 2024.
